summary:
# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (compact reference)

## BOOK 1 of 2: SKINNY McCORD (Percy Keese Fitzhugh, 1928; Grosset & Dunlap; illus. Howard L. Hastings)

**Setting:** Temple Camp, Black Lake, Greene Co., NY (founded by Mr. John Temple). Bridgeboro NJ is home troop city (First Bridgeboro Troop). Leeds = nearest village; Catskill = rail stop; Kingston = store where suit bought. Blythedale Boys' Home/reform school (Blythedale, near Tonley's Corners, Irontown earlier). Wave Crest City, Florida = Bently home.

**Main characters:**
- **Skinny McCord** (Alfred McCord): small, shy, bashful, "gnome," ~64 lbs, big staring eyes, queer shuffling trot, wears too-big scout suit (bought Kingston with Curry, not worn), patrol = Elks (Connie Bennett leader), mascot, Martha Norris Memorial Cabins. Lost tin compass (ch 1). Half-brother Danny's "hero." Sleeps w/ no shoes at times; shoes hung around neck.
- **Danny McCord** (Danny, "Danville M." initials "D.M."): older half-brother (different mother), escapee from Blythedale Home; knocked out Dick Kinney of Irontown for teasing Skinny; hit Vic Norris (ch 18) for "slum rat" insult; nonchalant, reckless, "Yere?", "Naah", "You should worry," "Tiny"/"kid" for Skinny. Pretends to be Danville Bently at camp (July 1–~July 15). Hides in switchman's shanty in overgrown railroad cut above camp. Father: Mr. McCord (paper mill job, Bridgeboro); sent $15 via letter. Expelled after two weeks; given $70 (balance $30 + $40 transport), returns $ to camp envelope; leaves on 6:32 train by hike. Later postcard w/ $10 postmarked Porto Rico.
- **Danville Bently** (real one; Roswell T. Bently, father; Wave Crest City FL; "Polar Bear" patrol, white scarf and belt, silver ring from sister; "Tent Village"): arrives Aug 2; the "real" boy, later "White Scarf"; takes Overlook Cabin on Black Hill; saves Skinny and Danny from cave; declines Gold Cross.
- **Roy Blakeley** (Silver Foxes; "jollier"), Pee-wee Harris (mentioned), Brent Gaylong, Tom Slade (camp assistant), Uncle Jeb (Rushmore, western trapper), Councilor Barrows, Councilor Wainwright ("Wainey"; admin), Councilor Tenny, Councilor Wallace, Mr. Ellsworth (Bridgeboro scoutmaster), Chocolate Drop (colored cook, "Massa Slade").
- Elks patrol: Connie Bennett (leader), Vic Norris, Stut Moran, Bert McAlpin, Hunt Ward, Cresswell-type others; Brent; Curry (asst. scoutmaster, drove Ford to Kingston).
- Holman Sharpe (New Hampshire pioneer scout, Pioneer Row, Pie Alley; "law one"/"law ten"; "Sophomore Senior Sharpy"). Ralph Warner, Warde Hollister (Silver Foxes; serenaded Holman).
- Helmer Clarkson (rich; figs/grapefruit; Alligators of Alleghany cabin with skunk skin; "Sweet-dream Ellie"); Hiawatha Prize canoe.
- Howell Cross (Vermont Eagles, Eagle Scout), Ellis Carway (Eagle), Holly Hollis (Eagle; Gold Cross refusal; Eagle race winner/ marsh rescue victim).
- Charlie Avery (Long Island), Pompy Arliss (Brooklyn).
- Dutch/"Henny's Cave" (seven miles; "Test Four"), Spook Falls, Outlet Brook, Valley Creek.

**Sequence (chapters):**
1. Skinny loses compass at camp-fire; teased; Tom, Brent, Uncle Jeb talk.
2. Stranger (Danny) waits on bench at road; letter from Bently's Hotel, Wave Crest City, Florida (dated June 27, 1927; Bently father Roswell T.; son to report Aug 2; check $ for August).
3. Danny finds letter; sees "Martha Norris Memorial Cabins. Up path from fire turn left—second cabin."
4. Danny at camp fire circle; Skinny appears ("That you, Tiny?").
5. Skinny leads to railroad cut shanty (red lantern, smelly oil, tomato can). Danny plans to escape (grape-vine, ice-tongs, Blythedale). Letter read; Danny proposes impersonation.
6. Danny decides impersonation; Skinny terrified; dog-threat.
7. Skinny steals locker items (scout suit, Handbook); Danny dresses.
8. Skinny steals white pennant from Elks-rival cabin (Vermont? Virginia troop) by creeping; runs.
9. Connie: midnight "put on your scout suit." Skinny swims at dawn to Hiawatha Prize (canoe); Administration Shack.
10. Fisherman rescues Skinny at shore; Connie, Stut, Doc Carson (Ravens first aid).
11. Skinny sells canoe offer to Helmer Clarkson ($15) at Alligators cabin; refused; "What a tragic word is IF!"
12. Scout Law Number Two; Danny in shanty reading Handbook.
13. Breakfast; Vic Norris insult; Ned/Danny punches Vic; Skinny confronted by Connie re canoe sale.
14. Mr. Ellsworth; Danny in Pioneer Row; Holman Sharpe introduced (Danny's room-mate).
15. Danny called to office; Councilor Wainwright; Roy's serenade ("Oh Sharpy, dear Sharpy").
16. Holman's argument; Ralph Warner slapped; Danny steps between.
17. Councilor Wainwright takes Danny; Danny takes blame; Danny expelled, paid $70.
18. Danny returns $70 in camp envelope; hikes away.
19. Danville Bently arrives (Aug 2, white scarf, Polar Bears of Florida); Tom Slade; Skinny guides him.
20. Bulletin notice re impersonation; Danville befriends Skinny; Howell Cross invites; "Alfred McCord."
21. Canoe tip trick; Elks yield canoe to Skinny.
22. Partners talk; Test Four plan; Skinny's lines ("Sunday School boys").
23. Henny's Cave hike; Danville & Skinny enter.
24. Smoke, Danville pulls out a boy (Danny) — Danville unconscious; Skinny missing.
25. Skinny's inspiration: digs hole with stick to vent smoke.
26. Skinny's leg bound by rattlesnake (rattler); plans tourniquet; shouts.
27. Danville saves: pins snake with jackknife into bark; Danny revealed as rescued; "Who's the guy you've got with you?"
28. Danville agrees to hush; $20; Danny leaves; Danville gives up Gold Cross; Elks cheat Skinny; Holly Hollis to replace Skinny's place.
29. Danny postcard ($10, Porto Rico); Danville refuses Gold Cross; Skinny "Eagle" talk; Elks ask for locker key.
30. Overlook Cabin (Black Hill) engaged by Danville; Hollis.
31. Overlook Cabin & signal easel described; Holly Hollis described.
32. Night before race: Eagle race; Skinny "patrol" talk.
33. Race: Elks shell; Hollis swamped in marsh; Skinny tears signal easel down as rescue canvas.
34. Holly resigns Elk patrol; Danville: "An eagle is nothing but a lot of merit badges"; "An Eagle is not as high as you can go." THE END.

Key lines: "Skinny weighed sixty-four pounds, not counting his heart." Skinny: "I got it, I got it!"; "Put on your scout suit"; "Who's going to stop us!"

**Ending** (Gold Cross meaningless to Danville; "What they don't know won't hurt them.")

---

## BOOK 2 of 2: WON AT LAST; or, MRS. BRISCOE'S NEPHEWS (Agnes Giberne; John F. Shaw & Co., London; New Edition)

**Narrator:** Marion Hazel (mother; née; fair, slight; "I"). Husband **Robert Hazel** (clerk, Peterson & Co., London mercantile; quiet, kind, careworn; grey streaks). Married ~18+ years earlier; age 22/18 at marriage.

**Children (nine in family, per narrative):**
- **Cherry** (Cherry, twin of Cress; ~16; plain, plump, short, smooth hair; "clean hands"; loving; peacemaker; Philippians 4:19 "All your need").
- **Cresswell "Cress"** (twin; handsome, clever, selfish, listless; wants college/barrister; later sent to India; Maimie's pursuer; struck Jack twice; "Maimie likes him best").
- **Jack** (eldest, ~19 later; tall, broad, honest grey eyes, slow in school, sunny; mother's favorite; tutored by Maimie; "I'll be a man"; idol issue; marries Maimie).
- **Owen** (~14; steady, slow; "Mother, she says she's our cousin").
- **Fred** (training ship later; Merchant Navy).
- **Robert (Bob)**, **Edmund (Ted)** (youngest; fair-haired; by mother's side).

**Other characters:**
- **Maimie Browne** (Mary; "Maimie"; age 14 at arrival, 17 at birthday in June; flaxen curls, black eyes, pale; "Aunt Marion" / "Uncle Robert"; "little dove"; teaches; inflammation/ measles; declines Gold? no—"Mrs. Jack Hazel" later). Father = stepfather **Churton Hazel** (Robert's younger brother; stout, black beard, loud; Canada → US → South Africa farming; "little dove"; selfish, wants inheritance).
- Maimie's mother (Mrs. Browne, died; "Mrs. Browne" letters).
- **Aunt Elizabeth Briscoe** ("The Gables," near London; widow of Uncle Briscoe; rheumatic gout; blunt, sharp; "Fudge!"; "Bosh"; garden/conservatory). Her two servants: new girl (Maria) & cook. Lawyer Mr. Wilson (grey, silent).
- Mr. Bowen (passenger); Mr. Morison (Jack's employer; Jack's foreman).
- Doctor (parish, elderly).

**Key dates/facts:** Letter to "Dear Niece Marion" on a Thursday (Aunt Briscoe writes Thursdays). Maimie arrives on a Thursday in late February. Saturday trip to The Gables. Hampton Court/ Bushey Park excursion on Maimie's 17th birthday (June; rowing trip). Five pounds from Aunt Briscoe. Churton's bank-note £25 (pounds). Churton's cheque £20. Codicils: Mrs. Briscoe's will left all to Robert; codicil (3 months before death) gave all to Churton and £500 to Robert; later codicil (~3 weeks before death) reverted, Robert gets all except £1000 to Jack. Aunt Briscoe died; telegram: "Aunt B. died this morning; paralytic stroke last night; unconscious to the last." Maimie ~ "Jack's wife" three years later.

**Events in order (chapters I–XXVIII):**
I. Cherry & Marion talk; Cress wants shoes; Cherry's old jacket; Jack's blunders; Robert's job.
II. Aunt Briscoe's letter (invites Robert; Jack; Cherry; Robert travels third-class). Maimie arrives: "Aunt Marion... my name is Maimie Browne"; Churton's marriage unknown.
III. Marion, Robert question Maimie; Maimie goes to sleep; "What to do with her?"
IV. Packet of letters (Churton's letters); Robert: "what if our Master gives it to us to be carried?"; Maimie sleeps on Robert's shoulder.
V. Visit to The Gables; Aunt Briscoe refuses money; "There's the Parish"; workhouse.
VI. Cherry: "All your need"; "Casting all your care"; Marion resolves.
VII. Late return from Westminster/St Paul's; Cress/Maimie; "little wife"/ "Hampton Court" hints; Marion warns Maimie.
VIII. Maimie does housework; Jack vs Marion; Maimie's side-pain; "Maimie, what's the matter?"
IX. Burdens: Maimie collapses; inflammation; Marion's failure in trust; jealousy.
X. Maimie's hospital wish; Marion holds Maimie; "Darling"; Jack weeps.
XI. Illness; Aunt Briscoe's £5; Maimie's clinging; Jack's blunder warning; Maimie: "Jack, may I ask a question?"
XII. Maimie tutors Jack ("can't" vs "will"); tables; history; Maimie teaches Bob & Ted.
XIII. Aunt Briscoe visits; questions Maimie; wants her for a week; Maimie leaves 7 pm.
XIV. Four weeks; Cress's job offer; Churton's letter with £25; "A home for Maimie"; Maimie: "This is home."
XV. Two years later; Maimie 17; Hampton Court excursion; Jack & Cress both devoted; Marion: "I have a horror of brothers being rivals."
XVI. Bushey Park: Jack weeping; Maimie's account of Cress's "little wife"; Maimie: "I love Aunt Marion."
XVII. Churton appears in the house (black beard); "Father!"; wants her; "I'll give you a cheque."
XVIII. Churton stays nearby; Jack & Marion talk ("Maimie is my idol").
XIX. Measles: Ted, Bob, Cherry; Maimie insists on helping; lung inflammation; Churton stays away.
XX. Churton's £20 cheque; Cress & Jack struggle; Cress strikes Jack; Maimie's arm bruised.
XXI. Robert talks to Cress; Cress wants to go away; India posting; The Gables locked; Marion suspects Churton.
XXII. Cress leaves (Feb); Jack's gift of Bible; Robert & Jack turned away from The Gables; Maimie resolves to write.
XXIII. Maimie's letter to Churton; Churton comes; Maimie: "Do I belong to you or Uncle Robert?"; demands; "half-an-hour" ultimatum.
XXIV. Maimie leaves with Churton to The Gables; "It is for Uncle's sake."
XXV. Robert visits Maimie; Churton present; Maimie's note given "Not a word to anybody else."
XXVI. Note (Maimie writes Aunt Marion: father pays no post; Aunt Briscoe says Robert offended her); telegram: Aunt B. died.
XXVII. Funeral; will read by lawyer Mr. Wilson; codicils; Churton furious; Maimie: "This is your doing?"; Churton renounces Maimie.
XXVIII. Maimie explains Aunt Briscoe; Robert inherits; move to The Gables; Jack proposes ("My own! my very own!"); three years later Jack & Maimie marry; Churton letter (South Africa; £5 "wedding-gift"); Cress best man. THE END.

**Key quotes:** "What a shame it is boys can't work!"; "Mother, she's our cousin"; "Casting all your care upon Him"; "I shall never never love you if you say such things"; "It is the cruel... Maimie"; "Bosh!"; "An Eagle..." (not this book); "Pray that she may never be my idol"; Maimie: "I'd rather marry Cress" (joke); "Jack, look happy again."
